entry.title: Games that occupied my life
entry.content:
Games are in fact occupation of childhood and adulthood. We pay with out time to play, form social community or just kill time playing it.

Early childhood

The best game that really filled my early childhood was GTA Vice City, the OG steal car and roam around, act as a simulator person immersed in Tony's grant adventure of theft

In fact, before this most of my time was spent on playing WWE SmackDown! Here Comes the Pain in PS2 with my brother and close friend. It used to be so fun, to smack and pin down people. In fact I do love WWE for its entertainment factor and character they had in Attitude era (that's for another blog)

GTA Vice City game showing final Mission Passed.

WWE Smackdown here comes pain, undertaker choke slamming Brock in Elimination chamber

Along with this, offline games that crushed my time were, Road Rash, yep kick the police guy and swing the chain and smash it right on the head.

Also Captain Claw was so good, cat and dog chase in such a pirated way, maybe this started my love towards Pirates world (One piece). Captain claw was definitely ahead of its time for sure, even today I find the visuals stunning compared to any mobile games.

Road rash game with cop chasing and one biker about to be kicked

Captain claw about to kill two puppy

Of course I cannot miss mentioning offline games outside in real life. With friends we also used to play cricket in the streets and in ground every day. School sports games weren't much though.

Adulthood

Most of the adulthood drifted towards using social media; Facebook was peak among socializing, Hike was crazy with stickers and there arised the mobile gaming which was at most peak.

As a kid the only game I discovered on android people playing was Subway Surfers and Temple Run, the endless runner that gave the dopamine a game needs to give. And at this time I had limited phone usage and time. Obviously I cannot forget the giant game that was on everyone's phone, Candy Crush Saga, it was just delicious.

Subway surfer where boy got caught by cop

Candy crush saga. The OG arcase puzzle game.

Then came the best game for mobile, Clash of Clans, it is the most nostalgic game that I feel even today. The slow base building, and clan socializing with players, constant chat, global chat to show off trophy leagues, war time, attach plans and Barchers attach, using each barbarian and archer to loot and save elixir, watch for efficient times on upgrades and so much more.

Clash of clans definitely felt more immersive to play and connect everyday to progress until TH11. TBH I liked until Th10, but TH11 gave night mare over an eagle for sure. After TH12 I think game went boring in bits and complicated the game. Until TH11 everything felt worth it and had its purpose in game. We friends and neighbors used to build clan, do attacks and discuss every day. Go to popular clan and ask for "Give me Co or else will leave", yes promotion was life achievement there.

Clash of Clans TH9 GoHo attack with hogs lvl 5 max

Clash royale training camp attack

Then game the big breakout with clash universe game, Clash Royale, which was easily best strategy game with cards and skills. It even beat out clash of clans in popularity and took over soon with esports scene and more. They had varied cards, various combos and it applied same clash of clans formula of being very immersive. But I wonder if it was supercell greedy or something, both games failed IMO after 2020, as they started complicating or people moved on with life.

In fact, clash royale was best those days, but soon in relaity later turned out be most regret mobile game to have wasted time on. Cause they ruined it so badly into Pay-to-upgrade tier.

Even tho brawl stars is kinda third success to them, I did not like brawl as it soon got complicated with pay to get easy upgrades stuff. Grind was totally bad.

But supercell definitely was the champ among mobile gaming and took over 2016-2020 until they complicated and ruined the games (thanks).

Pandemic

Then came the pandemic and home quarantine, this period started more time towards mobile gaming. Since all friends had to kill time, we eventually came to one game to play, it was Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB aka Moba Legends 5x5). This was 5v5 MOBA game which had several herous, flashy moves, skills and objective was simply to kill other players and beat the base.

This definitely took most hours player per day, and it was the first time which was totally competitive to play with others. We used to play as team and it was fun to curse, bash, troll and play many games laughing together.

Mobile Legends attacking in Enemy base

Onmyoji Arena, the beauty of MOBA game

Also there was one of the most beautiful and aesthetic game out there, which was not at all P2W and was the perfect MOBA for mobile, Onmyoji Arena. It had all japanese customs and themed, but thanks to Indian Gov, they banned all NetEase games, and flush it went away.

Obviously there was among us as well for a bit, but due to hype I started it, but not a major part of time occupancy.

Adult

After pandemic and MLBB, I slowly dropped playing any games. Our friends used to play Badminton together in park as beginner and slowly shifted to playing only in Indoor court nowadays (novice -> pro so quick!)

After that there aren't any games that made big impact or occupied tremendous time, all were offline or real life games.

Definitely I missed mentioning many misc games that once player, or simply enjoyed alone. Some of it were:

Detective games, Object finding games, Candy crush or farm saga, many puzzle solving games.

Recently I've been enjoying Honor of Kings the Chinese MOBA giant. Its better than MLBB for sure, but lacks the playerbase worldwide outside china, except that its a solid game with poor matchmaking.

As of writing this, I'm really enjoying Humbug 2 game, this is really fantastic puzzle game. Chill and cozy way to move insects to target.

Humbug 2 gameplay

Honor of Kings game

In case you wonder why no PC games are shown, PC was also used only for limited time. Now that I use Linux, I only have some casual native games here as well.

  1. Fishdom H2O: Hidden Odyssey - Detect objectives in cozy ocean
  2. Age of Empires and Age of Mythology (GOAT) - History speaks the strategy
  3. Need for Speed: Special Edition - The mclaren and the engine noise was bliss
  4. OpenTTD - FOSS Transport tycoon game

Fishdom H20 find hidden objects

Age of mythology village cooking

NFS SE Racing game

OpenTTD land mass

entry.title: Emacs on Droid
entry.content:
Emacs is a definite Greatest editor of all time, the extensibility power is unmatched with any other software. Users of Emacs can only know what it is, one who has not used it may not really understand the principles and power it gives us, the users.

Once settled with it on PC, its not late to think of something similar for our handy pocket phones, at least support for org-mode so we organize our life. The research leads us to find apps, and its unfortunate that market has lots of apps supporting markdown, just for its markup. Even org-mode is good for markup only, Karl voit's post explains it very well.

Finally we have some apps for org-mode, namely on Android Orgzly (maintained: orgzly-revived), Orgro (read-only app) and there is Organice (PWA site, unique, supports desktop). Surprisingly IOS has many apps for org-mode, namely beorg and plain org (I dont use IOS, so please search app store).

New project under development OrgNote also looks promising.

But it was near February, 2023, that Po Lu, one of the Emacs developer, started and released support for touch-screen devices (including Android) and to our surprise it was the graphical Emacs, available now on Android. But before trying the first doubts and cons expected was that it does not work well with virtual keyboard, so only good option is to carry physical keyboard everywhere? That could be solved by getting adjusted to keyboard app called "Hackers Keyboard" (TODO link).

But as I dug deep, the developer Po Lu, was on telegram channel in disguise, as I pointed that emacs android needed android's share feature (like open-with) to other people, he had seen it and implemented is very quickly. It shows how much of an interesting take-up it is.

Orgzly actually satisfied org-mode and agenda things with help of syncthing over org directory. But the next bummer came when I fell in love with Elfeed (RSS reader) and badly wanted to read feeds in sync with my phone. Since Emacs officially made its way for Android, so why not open some doors, indeed it did gave the power of emacs-lisp!

Initially I started with bare-bone config, and later tried to incorporate my PC config with android, and it was easy, without much hassle. Just had to define a constant to check if system is on Linux or Android, and use the keyword in condition statements and use-package. Next thought would be to use Unix tools/commands, so it only leads to Termux, and after few days, the developer released Termux signed apk to use in conjunction with emacs, so as to leverage the command line utilities in Android emacs too, namely ripgrep, git. I have not tried image-magick, mupdf for pdf-tools. But frankly Librera reader is good enough.

Here is a blog post by marek-g explaining how termux is modified to use with Emacs

Note: Fdroid emacs apk lacks some support like GnuTLS (so won't be able to install package or use eww), thus the only source to get emacs builds for Android is https://sourceforge.net/projects/android-ports-for-gnu-emacs

For anyone trying it out again or newly, please make sure you go through C-h R android or C-h r m android for frequent issues or things to know for Android build. For any queries to me, please feel free to open up an issue over this repo.

Overall with setting only few variables for android specifically, I replicated almost same emacs config on Android. The definite org-mode reader, read Elfeed feeds in sync with PC, whatever emacs packages you use.

Config just for android exclusively: 

;; define constant to check if system is android
(defconst d/on-droid (eq system-type 'android))
;; if system is android, executes following code
(when d/on-droid
  (custom-set-variables
   '(touch-screen-precision-scroll t) ;; smooth scrolling
   '(touch-screen-display-keyboard t)
   ;; ^ display virtual keyboard when touch on phone screen
   ;; does not work on read-only buffer (dashboard, startup..)
   '(browse-url-android-share t))
  ;; open links/urls with android's open-with or share kinda popup

  (defun d/key-droid()
    "To enable touch screen keyboard"
    (interactive)
    (frame-toggle-on-screen-keyboard (selected-frame) nil)
    )
  )

I'm not sure how suitable it is for coding environment (with lsp and complexities), but it behaves as expected for reading purpose and for quick note taking. I should probably say, it excels in that segment.

entry.title: FOSS : On Droid
entry.content:
As we know, Android is widely popular OS for many phone. But these days its all filled with junks and bloated apps, these are to say so called "Popular Android Apps" or "Trending Apps". The reason simply would be "everyone in my circle uses it" or "I use it because they use it".

But surely you are not giving yourself some privacy or space that you need for your own personal phone. I'm talking about using Free/Libre and Open Source (FOSS) Apps. Free doesn't mean by price, Free means Freedom. Freedom that comes with :

  • No Trackers.
  • No Ads.
  • Minimal permission.
  • Has customization to users need.
  • No Restrictions.

These can be achieved in this modern time, by Discovering and using FOSS Apps, the best place being F-droid or r/fossdroid.

There are pretty much all apps under FOSS area for every purpose, they are good looking with Modern UI, Lots of Customizations and friendly with Battery.

I happened to search for book and novel reader and found very good apps there, like QuickNovel. There is a Manga reader and lots more for every purpose.

I exclusively use every apps from F-droid, because they are great. You should also use it, as you might find something interesting and surely, gets Surprised; and say in your head, Gosh I should have known this before.

Some of the cool apps I use everyday :

Class Apps
Launcher Kvæsitso (izzydroid, git)
F-droid Client Neo Store (fdroid, git)
Browser Mull (fdroid, git)
Rss Reader Read You (fdroid, git)
YouTube LibreTube (fdroid, git)
PDF/Ebook Reader Librera Reader (fdroid, git)
Manga Reader Tachiyomi (fdroid, git)
Password Manager KeePassDX (fdroid, git)
Novel Reader QuickNovel (izzydroid, git)
Keyboard Unexpected Keyboard (fdroid, git)
Media Player VLC (fdroid, git)
Gallery + Calendar (many more) Simple Tools Suite (fdroid, git, site)
Note Taking Orgzly (fdroid, git)

With that fossed, I hope your phone gets a new life and finally breathes alive!
